problem: Automated skin-lesion classifiers achieve high aggregate performance but lack reliability for individual predictions, making it unsafe for clinical use without knowing when to trust a prediction.
method: Reliability-aware selective prediction framework: train transparent tree-ensemble classifiers with a lightweight, retraining-free reliability layer combining maximum class confidence, predictive entropy, post-hoc temperature scaling, and confidence/entropy-based accept–defer rules; evaluate on HAM10000 and ISIC 2018 datasets; assess calibration, error detection, selective prediction, and class-aware referral.
key_assumptions: Combining maximum class confidence, predictive entropy, and temperature scaling yields reliable uncertainty estimates for selective prediction.
main_contribution: A reliability-aware selective prediction framework that improves calibration (temperature scaling reduces ECE from 0.120 to 0.028), enables accurate error detection (AUROC 0.811), and supports deferral to experts; a malignancy-aware referral rule reduces melanoma miss rate from 26.9% to 7.6% at matched coverage.
datasets: Skin Cancer (ISIC 2018): Malignant vs. Benign dataset (3,297 images)
benchmarks: not explicitly stated; comparison with raw classifier performance
results: "On HAM10000, temperature scaling reduces expected calibration error from 0.120 to 0.028 (76.5% reduction). Accepting only the most reliable half of cases raises accepted-case accuracy to 0.905 while routing 83.7% of all errors to expert review. A malignancy-aware referral rule reduces the melanoma miss rate from 26.9% to 7.6% at matched coverage and below 1% at higher deferral. Similar trends observed on ISIC 2018 dataset."

relation_to_idea.conceptual_difference: The paper focuses on reliability-aware selective prediction for skin lesion classification using temperature scaling and confidence/entropy rules; the idea generalizes to calibrating any diverse set of models and using common thresholds for routing decisions in collaborative inference across language and vision tasks.
